title: 'Toaru Anbu no Item' Reveals Additional Cast, Promo
content:
The official website for the television anime adaptation of Kazuma Kamachi 's Toaru Anbu no Item ( A Certain Dark Side's Item ) light novel revealed additional cast and a promotional video on Saturday. The anime premiered on October 9 at 10.30 p.m. on AT-X, followed by Tokyo MX and BS11.

Cast Kaede Ibotanokikouji: Aya Yamane ( Kimi ga Shinu made Koi wo Shitai ) Kamitsu Hanayama: Yuuki Hirose ( Kowloon Generic Romance ) Laspezia Inoue: Konomi Inagaki ( Kirei ni Shitemoraemasu ka. ) Hiyoko Aiyose: Misaki Kuno ( Tenmaku no Jaadugar )

Tatsuyuki Nagai ( Toaru Kagaku no Railgun ) is directing the anime at J.C.Staff . Shougo Yasukawa ( Shokugeki no Souma ) is handling the series composition, while Shigeki Kimoto ( Dungeon ni Deai wo Motomeru no wa Machigatteiru Darou ka ) is designing the characters. Maiko Iuchi ( Akudama Drive ) is composing the music.

Kamachi began penning the spin-off light novel under the Dengeki Bunko imprint in March 2023, featuring illustrations by Nilitsu ( Shokei Shoujo no Virgin Road ). Kadokawa published the seventh volume on October 9.

Dengeki Daioh began serializing a manga adaptation by strelka ( Hinowa ga Yuku! ) in October 2023. Kadokawa released the second volume in April 2025.

PV (VS Item ver.)

title: Love Live! Hasunosora Anime Reveals New Trailer
content:
Love Live! Hasunosora Girls’ High School Idol Club anime revealed a new trailer on Saturday. The anime will premiere on January 10, 2027. Studio Sublimation is animating the series.

Go Kurosaki is directing the series, with Haruko Iizuka on character designs, and Yoshiaki Fujisawa on music. The voice cast consists of:

• Nozomi Nirei as Kaho Hinoshita

• Kokona Nonaka as Sayaka Murano

• Kanna Kan as Rurino Osawa

• Hina Sakurai as Ginko Momose

• Fuka Hayama as Kosuzu Kachimachi

• Rin Kurusu as Hime Anyoji

• Miu Miyake as Ceras Yanagida Lilienfeld

• Amane Shindo as Izumi Katsuragi

• Niina Hanamiya as Kozue Otomune

• Kona Tsukine as Megumi Fujishima

• Kotoko Sasaki as Tsuzuri Yugiri

• Julia Hoshimiya as Maika Kinjo

• Kana Asahi as Aoi Reisawa

• Kanae Yuasa as Mion Shinowa

The Hasunosora Girls’ High School Idol Club is part of the Link! Like! Love Live! project, which is centered around a smartphone application that launched on April 15, 2023. The members are introduced and developed within the app, which includes interactive storytelling, live 3D performances, and social media-style engagement with the idols. They made their musical debut with the song “Dream Believers,” which served as their first group single.

title: 'Re:Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu' Gets 5th Season
content:
The Re:Zero 10th Anniversary Starlight Party special event announced a fifth season on Saturday, revealing an ultra teaser visual (pictured).

Produced by White Fox , the first anime season adapting Tappei Nagatsuki 's isekai fantasy light novel debuted in Spring 2016, covering the first nine volumes. The Memory Snow side-story OVA premiered in theaters in October 2018, followed by the Hyouketsu no Kizuna ( The Frozen Bond ) prequel OVA in November 2019.

The second season aired in split cours, with the first cours airing in 13 episodes in Summer 2020 and the 12-episode second cours in Winter 2021.

The third season aired with the Shuugeki-hen ( Attack arc ) from October 2024 to November 2024. The Hangeki-hen ( Counterattack arc ) aired from February 2025 to March 2025.

The fourth season began airing with the Soshitsu-hen ( Loss Arc ) on April 8 and ended on July 17. The Dakkan-hen ( Recapture Arc ) aired from August 12 to September 30. Crunchyroll streamed the series with multiple subtitles and dubs.

Nagatsuki originally began penning the series on the Shousetsuka ni Narou website in April 2012. Kadokawa began printing the novel with illustrations by Shinichirou Ootsuka through its MF Bunko J imprint in January 2014 and published the 46th volume on September 25, with the 47th volume scheduled for December 25.

• Funimation originally licensed the anime series in North America and released the first season on home video in two installments in June 2018 and February 2019. Crunchyroll released the second and the third season on Blu-ray in September 2023 and July 2026, respectively.

Yen Press licensed the light novel in December 2015 and published the 29th volume on July 14, with the 30th volume scheduled for a December 8 release. The company also publishes the manga adaptations, the Re:Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu Ex ( Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World- Ex ) side novel and Re:Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu Tanpenshuu ( Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World- Short Story Collection ).

title: Re:ZERO Season 5 Anime Officially Announced
content:
Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World- Season 5 has been officially announced. An ultra teaser visual was also released. Tappei Nagatsuki also released a comment, which you can read below.

Congratulations on the production of Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World- Season 5! Congratulations! And thank you very much! I’m the original author, Tappei Nagatsuki! Season 5! What an incredible number! I have nothing but gratitude for everyone who has supported the series all the way to this point, and for all the staff and cast members who have continued to bring the story to audiences. And of course, that gratitude also goes to the characters who keep challenging their cruel destinies! The sixth arc covered in Season 4 has been called one of the most difficult parts of Re:ZERO, but don’t worry! The journey through the seventh arc is every bit as brutal, with the difficulty cranked all the way up to inferno. The story continues with the same reassuringly heart-breaking design you’ve come to expect—yes, “heart-breaking” is intentional! Of course, it won’t all be hardship. There will also be plenty of new encounters, exciting developments, and scenes I can’t wait to see—and show you—in anime form! Let’s make the journey ahead one that goes beyond anything you can imagine! Now then, Natsuki Subaru—the next battle begins! For Season 5, shake with anticipation and excitement together with the author as we wait!

The first season of the anime aired in 2016, adapting the light novel series by Tappei Nagatsuki and illustrated by Shinichirou Otsuka. The series announced 10 major projects for its 10th anniversary this year.

You can also see the Japanese version of the visual below:

The voice cast of the series includes:

• Kobayashi Yusuke as Subaru

• Rie Takahashi as Emilia

• Yumi Uchiyama as Puck

• Inori Minase as Rem

• Rie Murakawa as Ram

• Satomi Arai as Beatrice

• Kana Ueda as Anastasia

• Takuya Eguchi as Julius

• Fairouz Ai as Shaula

Season 4 of the anime also dominated the Spring and Summer seasonal polls. The staff of the 4th season consists of:

title: Gushing Over Magical Girls Season 2 Reveals New Visual, Trailer, 2027 Release Date
content:
Gushing Over Magical Girls Season 2 revealed a new visual and trailer that announce the 2027 release date.

The cast will reprise their roles for the sequel:

• Fuka Izumi as Utena Hiiragi/Magia Baiser

• Misato Fukuen as Venalita

• Aoi Koga as Kiwi Araga / Leopard

• Shiori Sugiura as Korisu Morino / Nero Alice

• Yuka Aisaka as Matama Akoya/Loco Musica

• Minami Tsuda as Nemo Anemo/Leberblume

• Kaori Maeda as Haruka Hanabishi/Magia Magenta

• Mayuko Kazama as Sayo Minakami / Magia Azul

• Misaki Ikeda as Kaoruko Tenkawa / Magia Sulfur

Asahi Productions animated the first season with Masato Suzuki and Atsushi Otsuki as directors. Noboru Kimura was in charge of the series composition, while Tomoka Otaki was on character designs and Yasuharu Takanashi , Akinari Suzuki, and Johannes Nilsson composed the music.

Gushing Over Magical Girls anime is based on a magical girl manga series by Akihiro Ononaka. It initially began its serialization on Takeshobo’s Storia Dash website in March 2019. J-Novel Club licenses the manga in English and they describe the plot as follows: “Hi, I’m Hiiragi Utena. I’m a normal magical-girl-loving middle school girl—or at least I was, but then some talking mascot showed up out of the blue and cast a spell on me! Now’s my chance to join my beloved magical girls as…a villain? Hang on, something’s wrong with my outfit! This can’t be happening! Watch this shy magical-girl fan transform into a sadistic dominatrix! When good and evil collide, who will be the one to submit?!”

title: Gushing Over Magical Girls Anime's 2nd Season Debuts in 2027
content:
Kadokawa revealed on Saturday that the second season of the anime based on Akihiro Ononaka 's Gushing Over Magical Girls ( Mahō Shōjo ni Akogarete ) manga will debut in 2027, under the title Mahō Shōjo ni Akogarete Season 2 ( Gushing Over Magical Girls Season 2 ). The new season was first announced in October 2024.

The company revealed the news in a birthday celebration video for Magia Baiser on Saturday.

Kadokawa also revealed an "ultra teaser visual," and confirmed the new season's returning cast and staff. The returning cast includes:

• Fūka Izumi as Utena Hiiragi/Magia Baiser

• Aoi Koga as Kiwi Araga/Leopard

• Shiori Sugiura as Korisu Morino/Nero Alice

• Yuka Aisaka as Matama Akoya/Loco Musica

• Minami Tsuda as Nemo Anemo/Leberblume

• Kaori Maeda as Haruka Hanabishi/Magia Magenta

• Mayuko Kazama as Sayo Minakami/Magia Azul

• Misaki Ikeda as Kaoruko Tenkawa/Magia Sulfur

• Misato Fukuen as Venalita

• Kana Asumi as Vatz

Masato Suzuki and Atsushi Ōtsuki are both returning to co-direct the anime at Asahi Production . Noboru Kimura is again overseeing the series scripts, and Yasuka Ōtaki is again designing the characters.

The first season debuted on the AT-X channel in January 2024, and the series also aired on Tokyo MX , BS11 , Sun TV , and KBS Kyoto . The anime has three different versions: the TV broadcast version, the "gushing" version on streaming services, and the "ultra-gushing" version on Blu-ray Disc and DVD. The TV broadcast version censors the audio and visuals, the "gushing" version censors the audio and some of the visuals, and the "ultra-gushing" version does not censor either.

HIDIVE streamed the anime as it aired in Japan, and has the series' "gushing" version available for streaming.

Ononaka launched the manga in Takeshobo 's Manga Life Storia magazine in 2019. After the magazine ceased publication in July 2019, the manga moved to the Storia Dash website.

The manga went on hiatus in March 2024 due to Ononaka's health, and resumed serialization in October 2025 on Takeshobo 's Takecomi! website .

J-Novel Club licensed the manga, and it describes the story:

Hi, I'm Hiiragi Utena. I'm a normal magical-girl-loving middle school girl—or at least I was, but then some talking mascot showed up out of the blue and cast a spell on me! Now's my chance to join my beloved magical girls as...a villain? Hang on, something's wrong with my outfit! This can't be happening! Watch this shy magical-girl fan transform into a sadistic dominatrix! When good and evil collide, who will be the one to submit?!

Takeshobo published the manga's 13th volume in Japan on September 16. The manga has more than 3 million copies in circulation worldwide, including digital copies sold.

title: 5 Classic ’90s English Dub Anime That Surpass the Originals
content:
The debate over which is better — subbed or dubbed anime — has persisted for years, but these English dubs streaming on Crunchyroll are some of the best in the game. Many anime fans are steadfast in the belief that all series should be viewed in their original Japanese forms. And there are plenty of reasons subtitled anime might be preferable to their dubbed counterparts. A lot can go wrong when dubbing a series, from the translated scripts not getting the story and dialogue right to voice actors missing the emotional mark. However, as anime has become more popular in the West, the quality of English dubs has improved, with studios putting more time, effort, and resources into their creation.

Some of the greatest English dubs are, sadly, not streaming on Crunchyroll as of this writing. Series like Steins;Gate and Death Note are known for their high-quality dubs, but they’re either not available in their entirety or aren’t on the streamer at all. Fortunately, there are still plenty of incredible English dubs to dig into, whether you’re experiencing these stories for the first time or looking to revisit them in another language. From a sci-fi anime about defeating tyranny to one of the most impactful titles of the ’90s, these are well worth your time.

5) Cowboy Bebop

Sunrise’s Cowboy Bebop takes place in a futuristic setting where humanity has begun to live out in space, and going right along with that has been a new wave of crime that necessitates the use of bounty hunters called Cowboys. Among those Cowboys are series protagonist Spike Spiegel and the rest of the crew of the Bebop , and the series follows their episodic adventures chasing after bounties to make a living while occasionally confronting the demons of their pasts. With its stellar writing, gorgeous animation, direction, and masterful use of Western themes in its writing and overall aesthetic, this anime stands out as one of the most unique and engaging anime of all time, with an incredible cast to flesh it out at every turn. Not only is Cowboy Bebop Shinichiro Watanabe’s most iconic anime, but it’s a series often considered one of the greatest anime of all time. Even after 25 years, it deserves to be recognized.

4) Trigun

As a sci-fi classic, Trigun was a bigger hit in the West compared to Japan, thanks to the Western inspirations behind the series. However, the original anime was significantly different from the manga, which is why a reboot was released much later. Since the franchise maintained a dedicated global fanbase throughout the decades, many ended up loving Trigun Stampede as well. The story follows Vash the Stampede, a man with an astronomical bounty on his head for being a merciless villain. Those who have only heard his name know him for being ruthless enough to leave a trail of blood in his wake. However, in reality, Vash is a soft-natured man who claims to have never killed a person and even hates violence.

3) Dragon Ball Z

Akira Toriyama’s Dragon Ball is one of the most influential anime and manga franchises of all time, which has inspired several mangaka to this day. The series popularized several Shonen tropes, such as transformations, which are still famously used in many series. While the original Dragon Ball anime set the foundation of the story, the sequel anime, titled Dragon Ball Z , played a crucial role in popularizing the franchise in the West. The story takes place four years after the events of Dragon Ball , where Goku is married to Chi-Chi and has a son named Gohan. However, his peaceful life is jeopardized when aliens from outer space threaten Earth and unveil Goku’s origins.

2) Yu Yu Hakusho

On the surface, Yu Yu Hakusho doesn’t seem much different from a majority of Shonen series that follow the protagonist’s journey after they gain newfound powers in the very first episode. However, there’s one thing that completely sets it apart from any other show. Instead of going through the conventional route of having the protagonist gain power after some unexpected encounter, the story begins with the death of Yusuke Urameshi. As a 14-year-old delinquent, he used to spend his days skipping school and causing trouble for those around him. He would even get into fights with his rival Kazuma Kuwabara. If that wasn’t bad enough, Yusuke would also ridicule his childhood friend Keiko Yukimura with every opportunity he got.

1) Outlaw Star

Space western anime were all the rage in the 1990s, and this theme is appreciated even to this day, as witnessed by the huge popularity of Cowboy Bebop . Unfortunately, Outlaw Star didn’t stand the test of time even though both series were released in the same year. While Outlaw Star is more or less forgotten among new anime fans, it still has a small but dedicated fanbase. However, this underrated gem was once one of the most popular space anime, loved for its intriguing adventure with a blend of fun and space exploration. The story follows a young man, Gene Starwing, who always dreamed of piloting his own ship across the galaxy, but has been stuck doing odd jobs with his partner James Hawking. The duo’s life takes a drastic turn after accepting a job from Rachel Sweet, who turns out to be a treasure-hunting outlaw. While Gene and James are only tasked with protecting Melina, a mysterious girl, they soon get entangled in more dangers than they bargained for.

contentBlocks.text: The debate over which is better — subbed or dubbed anime — has persisted for years, but these English dubs streaming on Crunchyroll are some of the best in the game. Many anime fans are steadfast in the belief that all series should be viewed in their original Japanese forms. And there are plenty of reasons subtitled anime might be preferable to their dubbed counterparts. A lot can go wrong when dubbing a series, from the translated scripts not getting the story and dialogue right to voice actors missing the emotional mark. However, as anime has become more popular in the West, the quality of English dubs has improved, with studios putting more time, effort, and resources into their creation.

Some of the greatest English dubs are, sadly, not streaming on Crunchyroll as of this writing. Series like Steins;Gate and Death Note are known for their high-quality dubs, but they’re either not available in their entirety or aren’t on the streamer at all. Fortunately, there are still plenty of incredible English dubs to dig into, whether you’re experiencing these stories for the first time or looking to revisit them in another language. From a sci-fi anime about defeating tyranny to one of the most impactful titles of the ’90s, these are well worth your time.
5) Cowboy Bebop

Sunrise’s Cowboy Bebop takes place in a futuristic setting where humanity has begun to live out in space, and going right along with that has been a new wave of crime that necessitates the use of bounty hunters called Cowboys. Among those Cowboys are series protagonist Spike Spiegel and the rest of the crew of the Bebop , and the series follows their episodic adventures chasing after bounties to make a living while occasionally confronting the demons of their pasts. With its stellar writing, gorgeous animation, direction, and masterful use of Western themes in its writing and overall aesthetic, this anime stands out as one of the most unique and engaging anime of all time, with an incredible cast to flesh it out at every turn. Not only is Cowboy Bebop Shinichiro Watanabe’s most iconic anime, but it’s a series often considered one of the greatest anime of all time. Even after 25 years, it deserves to be recognized.
4) Trigun

As a sci-fi classic, Trigun was a bigger hit in the West compared to Japan, thanks to the Western inspirations behind the series. However, the original anime was significantly different from the manga, which is why a reboot was released much later. Since the franchise maintained a dedicated global fanbase throughout the decades, many ended up loving Trigun Stampede as well. The story follows Vash the Stampede, a man with an astronomical bounty on his head for being a merciless villain. Those who have only heard his name know him for being ruthless enough to leave a trail of blood in his wake. However, in reality, Vash is a soft-natured man who claims to have never killed a person and even hates violence.
3) Dragon Ball Z

Akira Toriyama’s Dragon Ball is one of the most influential anime and manga franchises of all time, which has inspired several mangaka to this day. The series popularized several Shonen tropes, such as transformations, which are still famously used in many series. While the original Dragon Ball anime set the foundation of the story, the sequel anime, titled Dragon Ball Z , played a crucial role in popularizing the franchise in the West. The story takes place four years after the events of Dragon Ball , where Goku is married to Chi-Chi and has a son named Gohan. However, his peaceful life is jeopardized when aliens from outer space threaten Earth and unveil Goku’s origins.
2) Yu Yu Hakusho

On the surface, Yu Yu Hakusho doesn’t seem much different from a majority of Shonen series that follow the protagonist’s journey after they gain newfound powers in the very first episode. However, there’s one thing that completely sets it apart from any other show. Instead of going through the conventional route of having the protagonist gain power after some unexpected encounter, the story begins with the death of Yusuke Urameshi. As a 14-year-old delinquent, he used to spend his days skipping school and causing trouble for those around him. He would even get into fights with his rival Kazuma Kuwabara. title: Solo Leveling Studio’s Next Big Anime Is Everything My Dress-Up Darling Couldn’t Be
content:
Now that 2026 is approaching its end, the anime industry is getting ready for its upcoming releases for 2027, including a gorgeous anime from A-1 Pictures. This is the same studio behind Solo Leveling , and it’s known for several acclaimed shows. The studio’s latest project, Bless , is one of the most anticipated anime of 2027. It was already scheduled for the Winter 2027 lineup, and now that the season is closer than ever, the studio confirmed its release date in a new trailer. The gorgeous trailer sheds more light on the main characters before confirming that the anime will premiere on January 8th, 2027.

The official X handle of the anime also shared a key visual along with the confirmation that the episodes will broadcast every Friday at 11:30 P.M. on Fuji TV’s Noitamina network. The new trailer also introduces the cast and crew, along with a few new glimpses at the main characters. The anime has already gathered a lot of attention not only because of its visuals and unique premise, but also because the studio behind Solo Leveling is producing it, which is enough to pique fans’ interest. Established in 2005, this renowned studio is responsible for creating several modern classics such as Kaguya-sama: Love Is War , Your Lie in April , and many more.

Bless Challenges the Narrow Beauty Standards in the Fashion Industry

The anime is based on Yukino Sonoyama’s acclaimed Shonen manga, which began serialization in Kodansha’s monthly Shonen Sirius magazine in 2022. The story centers around 15-year-old Aia Udagawa , who has been chosen as a model for the Aoi Festival Artist Contest due to his previous experience. However, amid his inner struggles, he notices Jin Sumisaki, a tall and awkward girl who appears embarrassed about her appearance. The two of them are paired as a model and stylist, which becomes a major turning point in their lives. While Udagawa regrets abandoning his dream after convincing himself he has no talent, Sumisaki lacks the confidence to work as a model despite having the stunning features that make her stand out from the crowd. The story continues as the duo embraces their dreams while giving each other the push needed to break free from the shackles of self-doubt.

Bless Has a Better Story and More Emotional Depth Than My Dress-Up Darling

My Dress-Up Darling is a popular cosplay drama centering around Wakana Gojo, a high school boy whose hobby is crafting traditional Hina dolls, but he is socially awkward and afraid of people judging him. However, Marin, a popular and outgoing classmate, discovers his skills and urges him to help her out. As an avid cosplayer with no sewing experience, she seeks his help in making costumes. Despite contrasting personalities, they soon become friends, and Wakana learns to appreciate his talent more. Marin gets to try unique and creative cosplays. As the story continues, their relationship deepens, making the series a heartwarming and comedic story. Written and illustrated by Shinichi Fukuda, the manga was published in Young Gangan, a magazine owned by Square Enix Holdings. The manga debuted in January 2018 and reached its conclusion in March 2025. While the series has incredible reviews from fans and critics, it’s also highly controversial for its heavy use of fan service, especially since the character in question is a 15-year-old girl.

Bless is a truly unique shonen series. While the demographic is no stranger to series that dip away from traditional action stories and explore coming-of-age and slice-of-life themes, the narrative and themes Bless chooses to explore are things that are stereotypically attributed to shoujo manga. This isn’t a bad thing, either, as Bless is a masterclass example of storytelling in how it introduces its lead characters and explores the two of them navigating the makeup industry. Aia is a young man who aspires to be a makeup artist; while this isn’t as uncommon as it used to be, it’s still a relatively unconventional career path for a young man to pursue.

He enters high school decides to push his passion as deep down as it can go until he meets Jun, a reserved girl with a face covered in freckles who hides herself away due to her own insecurities. Somehow, Aia becomes captivated by Jun and convinces her to enter their school’s fashion competition together, with Aia doing Jun’s makeup for the show. The two make a powerful team and embark on a journey of self-discovery and personal growth as they begin to dominate the fashion industry in Japan. The series focuses on learning to trust and open up, and embracing every creative face of one’s personality.

Do you think Bless has what it takes to stand out more than My Dress-Up Darling ? And what are you most excited to see in its adaptation? Share your thoughts in the comments below.
